📝 Docs-Driven AI (Part 2): How to Write a ‘Blueprint’ YAML + Markdown to Control AI
In Part 1 the other day, we had a long chat about why the old way (typing random prompts) always makes AI confused and hallucinate. We also got introduced to the Docs-Driven AI concept, which is using a combined YAML and Markdown file as the “Blueprint” for our system.
Now, it’s time to get practical! Roll up your sleeves, open your text editor (VS Code, Cursor, or even Notepad works), and let’s build our first .md file. 🛠️
🔍 Anatomy of the Specification File (blueprint.md)
This file is super simple. It’s divided into two main parts. Remember this formula:
•
Top Section (YAML): Enclosed by three dashes ---. This is the Iron Laws (Metadata, Tech Stack, Database). AI must obey and can’t change it!
•
Bottom Section (Markdown): Regular text using headings (#) and bullet points (-). This is the Narrative (Business Logic, System Features, and User Interface).
💻 Practical Example: “TaskMaster” System (To-Do List)
Let’s take a basic example: We want to ask AI to help build a To-Do List app called TaskMaster.
Create a file named blueprint.md and paste the text below:
--- project_name: TaskMaster Pro version: 1.0.0 role: Expert Full-Stack Developer tech_stack: - Frontend: Next.js (App Router), TailwindCSS, Shadcn UI - Backend: Next.js API Routes - Database: SQLite (using Prisma ORM) database_schema: - model Task: id (String/UUID), title (String), is_completed (Boolean, default: false), created_at (DateTime) --- # 📌 System Summary This is a task management app (To-Do List) that allows users to add, mark as complete, and delete their daily tasks. # 🚀 Key Features 1. **Task Input:** A text field and "Add" button. 2. **Task List:** Display all tasks in a list format. 3. **Actions:** - Checkbox to mark task as complete. - "Trash" button to delete task. # 🧠 Business Logic (Business Rules) - Task `title` cannot be empty. If empty, prevent user from pressing the "Add" button. - If task is marked `is_completed: true`, the task text must be strikethrough and change to gray color. - Sort task list by `created_at` (newest on top).
Looks neat, right? All the technical info and business logic are laid out clearly. AI doesn’t have to guess anymore!
🪄 How to Use It (Prompting Strategy)
This is the most important part. Don’t just tell AI “Build this system”. AI will panic and try to spit out hundreds of lines of code at once (and usually fail halfway).
Use the “Step-by-Step Strategy”.
Open Cursor IDE, VS Code, Claude, or ChatGPT, upload the blueprint.md file, and input this sacred prompt:
“Please read and memorize this blueprint.md file. Understand the technical architecture, database schema, and defined business logic. DO NOT write any code yet. If you understand the full context, reply with ‘I UNDERSTAND’ and wait for my next instructions.”
When AI replies “I UNDERSTAND”, it means its brain is locked onto your blueprint!
Now, you can start directing it step by step:
•
Prompt 1: “Good. Now, please build the schema.prisma file based on the database_schema above.”
•
Prompt 2: (After Prisma is done) “Next, build the Frontend UI component for Task Input.”
🏁 Conclusion
With YAML Frontmatter + Markdown, you not only get to control AI more precisely, but you automatically have beautiful, organized project documentation. If next week you want to add a new feature, just update this blueprint.md file, give it back to AI, and continue working.
Stop being a tired “prompt typer.” Start being a smart System Architect who controls AI! 🚀
Happy experimenting, and share your experiences in the comments!
